Description: Neural Networks. The industry standard for dynamic realism. It reacts to your pick attack and volume knob roll-offs exactly like physical vacuum tubes.

Helix is component modeling oriented, aiming to match circuit stages and dynamic response. Helix models a pristine, "perfect" version of that circuit designed to sit perfectly in a modern mix with zero fuss.

absolute bleeding edge of component modeling. UA doesn't just model a schematic; they source a "Golden Unit" (the best-sounding physical amp they can find out of dozens), service it, and model its specific quirks. They model the exact transformer saturation, "cone cry" of the physical speaker, and the power supply sag of the specific tube rectifier.
When captures are done well, it can be scarily close to the specific rig state, but it’s fundamentally snapshot/capture behavior (knob sweeps aren’t “fully real” like a circuit model).

Softube secured the official endorsements from the hardware manufacturers. Their Marshall Plexi Super Lead 1959, for example, is the official, Marshall-approved digital version.Many of these models were developed in the mid-to-late 2010s. They still hold up incredibly well because the core math is excellent, but they lack the hyper-detailed speaker mechanics of the in-house UA plugins.

Brainworx amps sound incredibly "mix-ready" and tight, but some purists argue that their actual power amp modeling feels a bit stiffer under the fingers than Softube or in-house UA. You are relying heavily on their proprietary IRs (Impulse Responses) for the realism.
Agentic AI Engine. A massive leap for Positive Grid. The AI-assisted power amp saturation brings their realism up to par with professional studio modelers.

DIM™ (Dynamic Interaction). The VIR cabinet tech is stunningly realistic, though some older legacy amp models in the massive bundle can be inconsistent in their realism.

X-Gear --> Upper end (Top Tier Amplitube) "Finest Algorithm Ever"
Joe Satriani --> TONEX quality
Legacy Line 6 was POD era ports. Highly-refined, just old DSP technology.

Older Algorithmic Modeling. Shares its brain with BIAS Amp 2. It's incredibly versatile for live gigs, but side-by-side with Neural or TONEX, it lacks the complex intermodulation distortion and deep low-end thump of real iron transformers.

Older Algorithmic Modeling. Uses the same core engine as BIAS FX 2, but ranks slightly higher only because it allows you to literally swap the digital tubes, tone stacks, and transformers to chase a more accurate physical response.

Intelligent Circuit Modeling (ICM). The new ICM amps are a big step up in realism, but the audio community still largely views Guitar Rig as a creative, sound-design texture tool rather than a true replacement for a physical amp.

Fixed-Point Modeling. Released in 2023 for "instant tone gratification." It sounds great in a dense mix, but it lacks the micro-level component realism and deep touch-sensitivity of boutique modelers.

Legacy Digital. Built on very old technology. It is universally agreed to sound static and "fizzy" compared to anything built in the last decade.; user reviews frequently call it “plastic/fake” compared to modern sims.

“Good to have in Cubase,” but it’s a legacy-included amp suite (not generally considered top realism today). It is clean and reliable for demos, but it lacks the depth, power amp sag, and non-linear behavior of physical hardware.
